newsitem.title: USA: Duke postpones Oconee N.C. nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: Duke postpones Oconee N.C. nuke restart.

text.p: Duke Power Co has postponed the restart of electricity production at its Oconee nuclear power facility while investigations continue into the cause of a September accident, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
Duke said earlier it expected Oconee units 1 and 2, each with a capacity of 846 megawatts (MW), to resume power production in mid-November.
"That is not what we now expect," said spokesman Rick Zuercher, adding that ongoing investigations will push the startup dates back.
Specific restart dates have not yet been set for any of the three 846 MW units at the Seneca, N.C. plant, he said.

"We are continuing to evaluate a return to service date." Oconee unit 2 was shut September 24 after seven workers were scalded, four of them critically, when a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear part of the unit.
Units 1 and 3 were subsequently shut for inspections to ensure the same steam pipe problem would not occur there.
"A lot of the (current) inspections are associated with ensuring we don't have another problem like that," Zuercher said.
Oconee unit 3, also undergoing its scheduled autumn maintenance, had been expected to return to service in mid-December.
Duke Power has a total generation capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which the Oconee station accounts for about 14 percent.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
